newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai shares end up with crackdown shock over.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai shares end up with crackdown shock over.

text.p: Shanghai shares ended sharply up on Wednesday, with the B share index up 9.84 percent at 64.252 points, and the A index up 7.34 percent, and traders said investors were recovering from the shock of Beijing's stock crackdown this week.
The B share index closed up 5.754 points to 64.252 on volume of 37.1 million shares worth $1.4 million.
The A share index gained 69.525 points to 1016.241 on volume of 919.8 million shares worth 8.0 billion yuan.
"Investors are recovering from the shock after exchange officials and local media re-assured investors that Beijing would continue to develop the markets," one trader said.
The China Securities newspaper on Tuesday quoted the presidents of the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges as welcoming the crackdown, saying the markets needed stability to develop.
The newspaper also urged investors to be fully confident that the central government would continue to develop the stock markets on the basis of standardisation.
On the B share market, both domestic institutions and overseas investors built new positions in the belief that the impact of the crackdown would be limited, traders said.

Others also believed that B share prices were very cheap and would rise in the short term, traders said. One analyst said Shanghai's B shares on average were priced at only one-third the level of their A share counterparts.
B shares mostly ended limit-up with China Textile Machinery the most active stock on volume of 4.8 million shares.
Traders said the A share market trading was dominated by speculators who wanted to take advantage of plunges in the past two days to build positions.
Some retail investors, who had bought at higher levels, also built positions today to reduce the average cost of their shares, they said.

Quite a number of A shares closed limit-up today, mostly blue-chip stocks. Market giant Shanghai Petrochemical rose 0.50 yuan to 6.50 yuan on volume of 42.5 million shares, the day's most active stock.

"The markets might be over-speculative on the whole, but blue-chips have not been the target of excessive speculation," said one trader. "Shanghai Petrochmical, for instance, had a P/E ratio of only 18 percent against an average 40 on the market."
Traders believe that the B share market is likely to continue to rise in the next few days but the room for A share rises will be limited.
